maintenanceReason: The opt-in stratum-guided research harness (the bench-strata subcommand, the ockham/src/strata module and the strata_pilot example) has not earned ongoing maintenance. Its one synthetic real-scorer pilot was inconclusive: the aggregate, worst-stratum and pareto arms selected the same bundle on every seed, and the success criterion was not met for either treatment. No representative corpus was available. The predeclared rule in docs/strata-experiment.md tied removal to a representative run. That run has never been possible, so this record departs from the rule. The code was kept for it after the pilot. Replay at the pinned commit keeps the representative comparison runnable without maintaining the code. The removal is a maintenance decision, not evidence that the method fails on representative data.
negativeFindings: Synthetic real-scorer pilot, seeds 1 to 10: the aggregate, worst-stratum and pareto arms selected {d0, d1, d2, d3} on every seed. The arms are tied.
Worst-stratum minus aggregate, and pareto minus aggregate: every per-seed difference is 0 for validation delta, minority regressions and hidden neurons removed. The 95% interval is [0, 0] for each.
The criteria for worst-stratum and pareto are both met: false, with regressionReduction 0 against a required minimum of 1.
Worst-stratum minus random, validation delta: mean 4.755e-7, 95% interval [3.862e-7, 5.649e-7]. This is a comparison with a random control, not a benefit over aggregate.
No representative creature or corpus was available. The synthetic fixture cannot establish optimisation benefit.
